mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved monotonically for three weeks (-40.9, -40.0, -36.1, -34.3) while RETAIL_REC stagnated in a narrow -25 band. The transit recovery is the leading edge of mobility normalisation, and commuter-trip volume converts into discretionary retail footfall within four weeks, pulling RETAIL_REC above its trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 6.6 points from t-3w to t-0w while RETAIL_REC moved only 1.6 points
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT improves for three consecutive weeks, the forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is below the trailing 28-day mean in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has decayed from 8.7 to 7.3 across the four weekly means, showing households spending progressively less time confined at home. Once RESIDENTIAL prints below 7.3 the containment regime has loosened enough that trips reallocate from home to shops, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 8.7 at t-3w to 7.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its trailing 28-day mean within two weeks of the first RESIDENTIAL print below 7.3, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 7.3 while lockdown-type restrictions are re-announced.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved together (-40.9 to -34.3 and -38.7 to -32.0), which is the joint signature of restored commuting rather than leisure-only movement. Commuter corridors supply repeat discretionary visits to retail, so the coordinated rise, not either series alone, raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved in the t-1w and t-0w prints
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together for two weeks, the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the trailing mean, or the effect appears when TRANSIT rises alone with WORKPLACES flat.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS collapsed 17.9 points from 38.0 to 20.1 in the final week, ending the outdoor-leisure spike. The reallocation of leisure hours away from parks moves spending toward indoor discretionary venues, so RETAIL_REC rises within one week of the park reversal.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 17.9 points from t-1w (38.0) to t-0w (20.1)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS weekly mean drop greater than 15 points, or RETAIL_REC falls in tandem with PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improved 6.6 points into t-1w (-7.9 to -1.3) while RETAIL_REC stalled near -25. Supplies-led grocery gains with flat discretionary retail are the canonical signature of renewed non-essential restrictions, and the divergence drags RETAIL_REC further down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves more than 4 points while RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM gained 6.6 points from t-3w to t-1w while RETAIL_REC gained only 3.0 points
failure_condition: The forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is equal to or above the trailing mean after GROCERY_PHARM gains more than 4 points while RETAIL_REC remains flat.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS averaged 27.5 across the four weekly means, far above baseline, which identifies favourable outdoor weather and lengthening daylight. The same seasonal driver raises weekend discretionary shopping trips as well as park visits, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS mean over the four weekly prints is 27.5, above the zero baseline in every week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean is below its trailing mean while PARKS stays above +20 for every week of the four-week window.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES improved 6.7 points (-38.7 to -32.0) while RESIDENTIAL fell 1.4 points (8.7 to 7.3) in the same window, a joint return-to-office signature. Only the combination signals daytime population returning to commercial districts, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves and RESIDENTIAL declines in the same week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:from t-3w to t-0w WORKPLACES rose 6.7 points while RESIDENTIAL fell 1.4 points
failure_condition: The forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the trailing mean when WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week, or the effect holds when only one of the two moves.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC stayed inside a 3.0-point band (-26.9 to -23.9) for four weeks even as TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM improved, showing discretionary trips have been replaced by delivery habits that decay slowly. Habit persistence keeps retail footfall below its trailing mean over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC range across the four weekly means is 3.0 points while GROCERY_PHARM improved 5.5 points
failure_condition: The forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the trailing 28-day mean by more than 1 point while GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve.
